4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Throughout the inspection multiple food contact items were observed still soiled while in storage as ready for use. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator.

The dish machine in the facility could not, after multiple attempts, reach the critical temperature of 160°F at the surface of the dishes. Both inspector maximum registering thermometer and irreversible temperature indicator as well as the facility maximum registering thermometer were used. The PIC called EcoLab for maintenance and they stated that first thing tomorrow maintenance would commence. The three part sink was set up during this inspection with sanitizer. The dish machine can be used to wash and rinse the dishes and the sink used to sanitize. This is a temporary measure and a follow up will be conducted to ensure that the machine is effectively sanitizing again.

findings.comment:
Observed green beans and rice in the walk in cooler with no time stamp of when the cooling process began. PIC stated they had do not have a cooling policy nor were aware of one prior to this inspection. The proper cooling process was explained. Facility stated that they cool in two inch pans and food typically gets down to 40F within two hours. PHF should be cooled to 70F within two hours and down to 41F with an additional four hours. If PHF does not reach either temperature within the allotted time, food should either be discarded or reheated to 165F and begin the cooling process over. 
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.
